samples.question: This image shows one straight coloured post planted on a sloping hillside. The hillside is the large solid coloured area, and the straight line where it meets the white sky is the ground line. The grey page frame and the grey stones lying inside the hillside are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The post is always painted exactly along one of two directions, and only these two are possible. It is UPRIGHT when it is parallel to the left and right edges of the page, so that it makes the same angle with the page's top edge as those side edges do. It is SQUARE when it stands at a right angle to the ground line it is planted on, so that it leans by exactly the slope of the hillside. Which of the two it is, which way the hillside slopes, how steep the slope is, the height of the ground line, the two colours, the position of the post along the slope, and the post's length and thickness all change from image to image. Judge the direction actually painted in this image by comparing the post with the page edges and with the ground line, and do not answer from the direction a post normally has. Is the post upright or square? Answer with exactly one of the words upright or square.
